title: Western tour: Jim Crow hotels, John Williams cooking and bus trouble
summary: On a 1940 tour through Montana, Utah and Idaho the band stays in Chinese hotels and cooks its own food, and the bus fails in the mountains.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So we rode along beautifully, and in 1940 we decided to take the tour, so we went out west and I'll tell you it was pretty bad even then in 1940. Because we played all through Montana, Utah, Idaho, all out through there, and we couldn't stay in any white hotels or even in any white EAT
Oh, we also had John Williams who played baritone saxophone. He was one of the original 12 Clouds of Joy, and he's also -- was Mary Lou Williams' first husband.

He married her when she was 14 years old. Yes. And so he was in the band, and he's a great cook so we brought a big hot plate, and the only hotel we could stay in was a Chinese hotels out there and we had to cook our own food. And John would put these pots on for us every day and man we ate, we ate. Well, we was what you call sort of stranded in a way, but we did have --

We had Earl's car, and this little old bus that we had chartered. I'll tell you, when we got into Denver, Colorado going out to the west coast, we had played a dance and we left Denver to go to Sacramento, California. And that seemed like about 1500 miles, and look, we were riding along this highway and we said -- we're giving the bus driver hell saying come on, man, and drive the bus. We said, look, we don't have two or three days to get there, man, I mean, at the rate you're going. He says I've got to accelerate to the floor now.
Well, you see, this was a steady incline but it was so

slight until it looked straight. But this little bus -- you know, they had these big diesels passing us like mad out there, this mountain whipped this bus. And we would get up into the mountains we all would have to get out and push it up curves around some of these curbs, you know. It just couldn't make it. And then we messed all of the transmission up trying to do this thing with this bus.
